items.note: The projects filter field holding 'Apollo' has an ink border with the pink halo ring and a clear ×. The table drops to the single match and the count reads 'Showing 1 of 8 projects', so it is clear what the filter did. The other field and the controls stay ink-outlined and flat.

Same state on the near-black ground: the focused filter field shows a pink halo around a paper-bordered input, and its text is readable. The one-row table and the '1 of 8' count make the result obvious. The teal band keeps ink text.
At phone width the filter field keeps its pink halo, ink border and clear button. The table below reflows to one stacked block with the arrow row action, and nothing overlaps or is cut off.
The hovered first row takes a subtle gray fill with no lift, as the spec asks. The arrow row actions stay as small outlined ink boxes, and the rest of the table is unchanged.
In dark the hovered first row is only a slightly different shade from its neighbours, which is faint but present. The table keeps paper rules and outlined status pills, and every label is readable.
The first stacked row block shows the gray hover fill under its title, meta lines and arrow button. All eight blocks keep their labels inside the borders, with no lift on the row itself.
The focused 'Projects' sidebar pill shows a clear ink outline ring next to the ink-filled current 'Overview' pill. It is designed, not a browser default, and it is easy to see which item has focus.
In dark the focus ring on the 'Projects' pill is pink, clearly separate from the paper-filled current pill. The ring is readable against the dark sidebar.
The 'Projects' pill in the mobile top nav carries an ink focus outline beside the ink current pill. Nothing else on the page changes, and the outline is not clipped.

The user menu opens as a raised paper panel with an ink border and a hard offset shadow, under the user trigger. It lists the email, Account settings, My team and Sign out. It sits over the band edge without hiding any band text, and the trigger is not pink.
In dark the menu is a raised dark panel with a light border and the light hard shadow. Its items are readable, and it covers only the band's empty top-right area.

At phone width the menu drops from the avatar button as an outlined panel with the hard shadow. It covers part of the band title and the Refresh button, which is normal for an open overlay, and its own items are fully readable.

With 'zzzz no match' in the haloed filter field, the table becomes an outlined empty box. It holds a small magnifier sticker, 'No projects match your filters', one sentence of advice and a single pink 'Clear filters' button, the only pink action in view.
Same empty box on the dark raised card: readable heading and hint, one pink Clear filters button, and a pink halo on the field. The count reads '0 of 8'.
At phone width the empty box stacks the sticker, the heading, the hint and a pink 'Clear filters' button below the haloed filter field. Nothing is clipped, and there is a single pink action.

The stat cards read 'Loading...' and the band's Refresh button shows a small turning coin with 'Refreshing...', which is readable. But the button that is ink-outlined at rest turns into a pink fill while busy, on the teal band.

In dark the stat cards say 'Loading...' and the band button is again a pink 'Refreshing...' box with the coin. It is readable, but it is pink where the page-header action should stay ink or ghost in every state.
At phone width the band's Refresh button becomes a pink 'Refreshing...' block with the coin, and the four stat cards show 'Loading...'. The text is readable and nothing overlaps.

The only drawing is the throughput bar chart: flat raised-paper bars with 1px ink outlines, an ink baseline and one pink bar for the current month, with no gradient. It reads clearly as a bar chart at its size and fits the reference's flat outlined look.

findings.summary: While refreshing, the page-header Refresh button changes from its ink-outlined ghost look to a solid pink fill, in light, dark and mobile. The spec says an action that stays in a band or header is ink or ghost in every state. The ghost hover rule that flips the fill to pink doesn't exclude busy or disabled buttons, and that is what produces this. The label and the turning coin stay readable, and no other pink action is in view.
